{
  "pattern_id": "P-LIT-PRIORITIZE",
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "rationale": "The pattern P-LIT-PRIORITIZE aims to reorder tests to provide earlier failure feedback. In this workflow, the 'codespell' check is a single action. To implement the mechanism of prioritization within the constraints of a single-action workflow, I am splitting the check into two stages: a 'fast' check on a subset of critical files (simulating prioritization) followed by the full check. This adheres to the instruction to implement the mechanism even if the benefit is uncertain. I also added a caching step for the codespell cache to optimize performance, keyed by the runner OS and the pyproject.toml file as the dependency manifest.",
  "workflow_yaml": "# Codespell configuration is within pyproject.toml
---
name: Codespell

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  codespell:
    name: Check for spelling errors
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Cache Codespell
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .codespell_cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-codespell-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}

      - name: Annotate locations with typos
        uses: codespell-project/codespell-problem-matcher@9ba2c57125d4908eade4308f32c4ff814c184633

      - name: Prioritized Codespell (Fast Check)
        run: | 
          codespell --include-paths docs/ Makefile
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Codespell
        uses: codespell-project/actions-codespell@8f01853be192eb0f849a5c7d721450e7a467c579
"
}
